newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks rise on move to lift foreign ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks rise on move to lift foreign ceiling.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose strongly on Wednesday on global funds' buying of popular blue chips which are expected to benefit from an imminent decision to lift the ceiling on foreign ownership of shares, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.32 percent to 166.87 points on turnover worth 1.95 million dinars ($2.8 million).
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the index to a three-year high earlier in July, rose 7.00 dinars to 296 dinars in trade of 2160 shares.

Turnover in the bank's shares, worth some 637,310 dinars, dominated the market, riding the wave of optimism that the cabinet will soon approve the cancellation of the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling on most publicly listed shares.
The stock had fallen recently on selling by investors tired of waiting for approval of the change, already decided by the top government investment body earlier this month.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, the announcement of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.

Jordan Islamic Bank, another bank which has exceeded the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling and is widely believed to be a potential beneficiary of the ruling, rose 0.09 dinars to 3.91 dinars on large turnover of 185,704 dinars.
Overall, 30 shares rose on Wednesday, six fell and nine ended unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, rose 0.84 percent to 81.16 points, 2.67 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
